q: Which enzyme couples iodotyrosines into T4?
x: Thyroid peroxidase oxidizes iodide, iodinates tyrosines on thyroglobulin and couples DIT with DIT to form T4, all at the apical membrane; thionamides block it.

w.5'-deiodinase: Deiodinase removes iodine to convert T4 into T3 in tissues; it acts after secretion, not during coupling in the colloid.
w.Thyroglobulin protease: Lysosomal proteases cut finished T4 and T3 off thyroglobulin after endocytosis; coupling has already happened.
w.Sodium-iodide symporter: The symporter only traps iodide at the basolateral membrane; it has no enzymatic role in iodination or coupling.
w.Tyrosine hydroxylase: Tyrosine hydroxylase starts catecholamine synthesis; thyroid hormone is built by iodination, not hydroxylation.

pt.say: Thyroid peroxidase sits on the colloid side, where iodination and coupling happen.

q: Which hormone form binds the nuclear receptor most avidly?
x: T3 binds the thyroid hormone receptor with about ten times the affinity of T4, so tissues convert T4 to T3 before it acts.

w.T4: T4 is the main secreted form but binds the receptor weakly; tissues must deiodinate it to T3 first.
w.Reverse T3: Reverse T3 is an inactive product of inner-ring deiodination that rises in severe illness.
w.Thyroglobulin: Thyroglobulin is the storage scaffold in the colloid and never leaves the follicle in useful amounts.
w.TSH: TSH acts on a cell-surface G protein-coupled receptor on follicular cells, not a nuclear receptor.

pt.say: Coupling MIT with DIT makes T3, the form the nuclear receptor binds best.

q: What raises total T4 but leaves free T4 normal?
x: More thyroxine-binding globulin, as with estrogen or pregnancy, binds more T4; the gland makes extra until free T4, and so TSH, are normal again.

w.Graves disease: Graves antibodies raise free T4 and suppress TSH, so the free hormone is high, not normal.
w.Iodine deficiency: Iodine deficiency lowers hormone synthesis, raising TSH and eventually lowering free T4 and total T4.
w.Central hypothyroidism: Central hypothyroidism lowers free T4 with a low or normal TSH; total T4 falls rather than rises.
w.Amiodarone toxicity: Amiodarone can cause hyper- or hypothyroidism, changing free T4, and it blocks deiodination rather than binding proteins.

pt.say: The follicles are normal; the extra thyroxine-binding globulin comes from the liver, not the thyroid.
